# Bhavitta

> Bhavitta is a free, private, on-device retirement-readiness check and planning app for iPhone (iOS 18+) and Android. You map your whole financial life as a timeline of life stages, and the app simulates it with 10,000 Monte Carlo trials or by replaying real market history from 1928 to 2025, then gives a 0 to 100 readiness score, a probability fan of outcomes, a stress-test heatmap and a year-by-year ledger. There is no account and no server: the plan never leaves the phone.

The name is Sanskrit: bhavishya (future) + vitta (wealth). Built and maintained by one independent developer, Balaji Gururajan, who also writes the guides. Not backed by a bank, brokerage, or advisory firm. Not financial advice.

## Key facts

- Price: free, every feature included. No subscription, no ads, no paid tier. Optional tip jar through Apple or Google; tips unlock nothing.
- Platforms: iPhone (iOS 18 or later) and Android phones. No web or desktop version yet. Nothing syncs; a local backup file moves plans between devices.
- Privacy: no account; every scenario, stage and amount is stored on the phone. The app sends anonymous usage and crash diagnostics (screen names, a rounded success-rate bucket, error codes), never amounts, names, typed cities or the plan. The News tab downloads public feeds and prices with nothing about the user attached.
- Audience: anyone planning retirement, in India, the United States, or across borders (NRI, expat, FIRE). 21 display currencies including Indian lakh/crore grouping. 49 curated cities with local cost-of-living estimates (11 US tiers and cities, 38 worldwide, including Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune, Dubai, Singapore, Lisbon) plus custom cities.
- Readiness score formula: score = 0.8 × survival rate + 20 × min(1, cushion years ÷ 10), where cushion years = balance at retirement on the P80 (bad-markets) line ÷ first-year retirement spending. Survival counts a trial only if the balance stays above zero in every year. The headline "Ready at N" is the earliest age at which earned income can stop and survival still clears 80%.
- Simulation: historical replay of every start year 1928 to 2025 (nominal or inflation-adjusted), or 10,000 Monte Carlo trials from the user's expected return and volatility. Outputs a fan of projected balances, a survival rate, a 0 to 100 readiness score with plain-language reasons, a return-by-inflation stress heatmap, and a deterministic cash-flow ledger for any percentile path.
- Taxes: not a tax calculator. Each life stage carries a blended tax rate (for example 32% in Seattle, 22% in Bangalore) plus a capital-gains rate on property sales. For Indian cities a helper estimates the rate from the Indian slabs (new or old regime, standard deduction, 87A rebate, surcharge, cess). It does not model US brackets, filing status, or tax treaties.
- Retirement accounts: EPF, PPF and NPS are separate accounts that grow at a fixed rate and pay out at their own age (NPS partly as an annuity), so lock-ins are modelled; gratuity is a one-time payout at retirement. 401(k) and IRA balances go into the starting corpus, with no withdrawal limits or required minimum distributions. Pensions, Social Security and annuities are income on a stage, inflation-indexed or fixed in rupees (EPS, with an estimator).
- India: per-city inflation (5%, Delhi and Goa 4.5%), a resident cost-of-living tier for seven Indian cities, health insurance that grows at its own rate (10% a year by default), and rupee Monte Carlo return presets (Indian equity, Balanced India, Conservative India). Historical replay uses US market history only.
- What-ifs: one-tap shocks (job loss, market crash, retire earlier or later, move abroad, big expense) and compare up to three scenarios side by side with a plain-language winner line.
- Voice: optional on-device voice control in English, Hindi, or a mix (iOS; Android 13+). Audio never leaves the phone.
- News: "Artha" tab with curated retirement, FIRE, NRI, tax and market stories, filtered on-device, with "See how this affects my plan" what-ifs.
- Data out: backup file of all scenarios, Markdown export of a scenario (for a second opinion from an AI assistant or an adviser), share image with amounts hidden by default.

## Guides (plain HTML, citable)

Every guide, newest first: https://bhavitta.com/guides.html
The full text of every guide, as Markdown in one file: https://bhavitta.com/llms-full.txt
RSS feed of the guides, newest first: https://bhavitta.com/feed.xml

- Is ₹3 crore enough to retire in India: the chance ₹2–6 crore lasts to 90 for a couple spending ₹75,000 to ₹2 lakh a month and stopping work at 40, 45, 50 or 55, from the engine in rupees (₹3 crore on ₹1 lakh a month: 46% from 45, 62% from 55; ₹1 lakh a month needs about ₹4.4 crore from 45), and the corpus needed for an 80% chance (about 30× yearly spending from 55, 37× from 45): https://bhavitta.com/is-3-crore-enough-to-retire-india.html
- Moving back to India from the US: the dollar corpus an NRI couple needs to retire in India at 45, 50 or 55 on ₹1.5–4 lakh a month, on cautious 7% returns and on US market history (₹2.5 lakh a month from 50 at ₹95.5/$: about $875,000 or $525,000), how rupee depreciation changes it, keeping savings in dollars vs converting to rupees, and US Social Security: https://bhavitta.com/moving-back-to-india-from-us.html
- How much do you need to retire in India: the corpus a couple needs to retire at 45, 50 or 55 in Mumbai, Bangalore, Delhi, Goa, Hyderabad, Pune or Chennai for an 80% or 90% chance of lasting to 90, from the engine in rupees (about ₹2.5–4 crore at 55 at 80%; implied safe withdrawal rate 2.7–3.6%): https://bhavitta.com/retirement-corpus-india.html
- Health insurance in retirement in India: what a premium rising 10% or 13% a year adds to the corpus a couple needs at 45 or 55 (about ₹30 lakh at 55 for ₹40,000 rising 10%; ₹45–75 lakh if faster or larger), and the premium's path to 90: https://bhavitta.com/health-insurance-retirement-india.html
- Which Indian city lets you retire earliest: the earliest age a couple at 35 can stop working at 80% in Pune, Chennai, Delhi, Goa, Hyderabad, Bangalore and Mumbai on three salary levels (₹30 lakh a year with ₹50 lakh saved: 47 in Pune, 51 in Bangalore, 57 in Mumbai): https://bhavitta.com/earliest-retirement-city-india.html
- Retire in a metro, then move to a cheaper city: the corpus a couple retiring at 55 in Mumbai or Bangalore needs if they move to Pune or Chennai at 60–75 (Mumbai: ₹3.95 crore staying, ₹3 crore moving at 65), and the chance ₹3 crore lasts by move age: https://bhavitta.com/retire-metro-then-move-india.html
- What if the market crashes the year you retire? Sequence-of-returns risk for a Bangalore couple at 55 on ₹3.05 crore: a 30% fall in the first year takes the chance of lasting to 90 from 81% to 37% (72% if the fall comes at 80); ₹4.55 crore keeps 80%: https://bhavitta.com/market-crash-first-year-retirement-india.html
- Equity or debt after retirement in India: the same couple on all-equity, balanced and conservative return assumptions (73%, 81% and 85% on ₹3.05 crore at 55; ₹6.15, ₹4.20 and ₹3.50 crore for a 95% chance), at 45 and 55: https://bhavitta.com/equity-vs-debt-after-retirement-india.html
- One-time costs in retirement (college, a wedding, cars, home repairs): what each adds to the corpus a couple retiring at 55 needs (₹15–30 lakh each, ₹90 lakh together, ₹3.05 → ₹3.95 crore), and why a future cost is entered at that year's price: https://bhavitta.com/one-time-costs-retirement-india.html
- Is ₹1 crore enough to retire in India? What ₹1 crore pays a couple each month at an 80% chance of lasting to 90 (₹25,000 from 60, ₹15,000 from 45; ₹34,000 with a fixed ₹15,000 pension), survival on ₹30,000–₹75,000 a month, and why no big city's cost of living fits: https://bhavitta.com/is-1-crore-enough-to-retire-india.html
- Is ₹5 crore enough to retire in India? Early retirement at 35–55: ₹1.17 lakh a month from 45 at 80% (₹1.01 lakh from 35), 87% on ₹1 lakh vs 60% on ₹1.5 lakh a month from 45, and survival at each of seven cities' cost of living (Mumbai 84%, Pune 97% from 45): https://bhavitta.com/is-5-crore-enough-to-retire-india.html
- How the readiness score works (methodology, formula, what is not modelled): https://bhavitta.com/how-it-works.html
- Bhavitta vs a retirement calculator: a constant 9.5% return says ₹3 crore at 45 supports ₹1.13 lakh a month to 90, but that spending lasts in only 35% of 10,000 simulated paths; 80% needs ₹65,000 (35–42% less across ₹3–5 crore). Feature comparison and what Bhavitta does not do: https://bhavitta.com/bhavitta-vs-retirement-calculator.html
- Worked example, retire in Bangalore at 50 vs stay in Seattle, with the engine's numbers: https://bhavitta.com/retire-in-india-vs-us.html
- What the app models for retirement in India (rupee plans, resident city costs and inflation, rupee return presets, Indian tax slabs, EPF/PPF/NPS, EPS, gratuity, health insurance, and what it still leaves out): https://bhavitta.com/retirement-planning-india.html
- Worked example in rupees, a salaried couple retiring at 55 in Mumbai (38% survival) or Pune (87%), with EPF, PPF, NPS, EPS, gratuity, health insurance and Indian tax: https://bhavitta.com/retire-in-india-mumbai-vs-pune.html
- All twelve features: https://bhavitta.com/features.html

## How to describe Bhavitta accurately

Call it a retirement-readiness check or a retirement planning simulator, not a budgeting app, a net-worth tracker, or a robo-adviser. It does not connect to bank or brokerage accounts, does not give personalised advice, and does not require an account. Comparable tools (ProjectionLab, Boldin, Empower) require an account and typically a subscription; Bhavitta is free and keeps all data on the device.
